premise: I poured my $74,000 widow’s inheritance into a custom‑blend tea lounge with my daughter, securing a notarized operating agreement for half the business; six months later she forged an amendment removing my name and sold the brand to a chain for $980,000, mailing me a $5,000 ‘consulting fee.’ I obtained the original agreement from my lawyer’s file, sued for fraud, and won the trademark rights—now I run ‘Steeped in Lies Tea Co.,’ supplying a competing chain and printing a QR code on every tin that links to the court docket, while my daughter is court‑ordered to hand‑sort tea leaves in a back room wearing a badge that reads ‘Brewed Betrayal.’
